page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8369HB cores operating at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the ecs.c4.2xlarge in the average tier for most compute tasks. It achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1575.79 and a multi-core score of 8310.78. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16) and AES cryptography, which assist in encryption and vector processing. However, memory performance shows some limitations; while cached small-block read bandwidth is strong at 464.83 GB/sec, the uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to a weak 37.74 GB/sec. Similarly, the PassMark memory score and database operations benchmarks fall into the bottom 25% tier.

Given its compute-heavy configuration and lower memory-to-core ratio, this instance is suited for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. Appropriate use cases include web serving, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by its poor performance on medium 7B parameter models. Qualitatively, the instance offers a cost-efficient profile for dedicated compute tasks where local storage is managed externally and memory requirements are modest.
